questions.q: Why does the lesson say governance questions become important once an agent moves from a demo to production?
options: Because Copilot Studio stops working after a fixed number of test conversations
Because a published agent may read sensitive data, call connectors that touch real business systems, and propose actions with real consequences, unlike a single test agent only the builder talks to
Because production agents are technically a different product from Copilot Studio
Because governance only applies to agents built with the GitHub Copilot harness
questions.explain: A private test agent is low-risk because only its builder interacts with it. A published agent reaching real employees or customers has a meaningfully larger risk surface, which is why governance controls matter at that point.

questions.q: What does a data loss prevention (DLP) / data policy control in this context?
options: How many slides a lesson can have
Which connectors and capabilities agents in a given environment are allowed to use
The color scheme of a published agent's chat window
Whether a flow can be tested in the Copilot Studio designer
questions.explain: Data policies, configured in the Power Platform admin center, govern which connectors and capabilities are available to agents built in a given environment — for example, preventing use of an unapproved external connector.

questions.q: What does the agent inventory provide to IT and security admins?
options: A way to automatically rewrite an agent's instructions
A centralized view of every agent in the tenant, including who created it, when it was last published, and how it authenticates users
A list of every quiz question used across the course
A billing discount for agents published before a certain date
questions.explain: The agent inventory gives admins a tenant-wide, centralized view of agents and key metadata like creator, last published date, deployed channels, and authentication method.

questions.q: What is the recommended pattern when more than one agent needs the same capability, such as looking up a shipment by tracking number?
options: Rebuild the same logic separately inside every agent that needs it
Build the capability once as a shared agent flow and attach it as a tool to every agent that needs it
Only one agent per tenant is allowed to use any given capability
Capabilities cannot be shared between agents under any circumstances
questions.explain: Building a shared agent flow once and attaching it as a tool to multiple agents avoids duplicating logic — the same reuse instinct taught for flows back in Chapter 1.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend separate dev, test, and production environments for agents?
options: Because Copilot Studio requires exactly three environments to function at all
Because it lets you build and test an agent before it reaches real users, with data policies that can be looser in test and locked down in production
Because each environment uses a completely different, incompatible version of Copilot Studio
Because agent flows cannot be published more than once
questions.explain: Separating environments mirrors how a Power Automate solution matures: build and test in a non-production environment with its own (often looser) data policies, then publish to a locked-down production environment.
